codeReview.summary: The implementation correctly replaces the six targeted actor-side silent drops with `ctx.Unhandled()` and limits `ctx.Err()` to fatal configuration errors, but the new non-blocking email retry flow breaks Ask/Response semantics. Because retries are rescheduled without preserving the original sender, any email send that needs a retry will cause the calling grain to time out, so VAL-AS-005 is not actually satisfied.

issues.description: `handleEmailDispatch` reschedules retries with `ctx.ActorSystem().ScheduleOnce(ctx.Context(), retryMsg, ctx.Self(), delay)` but does not preserve the original sender/reply context (for example via `actor.WithSender(ctx.Sender())`). The later `ctx.Response(...)` therefore runs against the scheduled self-message instead of the original Ask caller. Since auth flows invoke the email actor with `ctx.AskActor(..., emailDispatchTimeout)` at `backend/janus-api/internal/actors/grains.go:197-210` and `261-274`, any send that requires a retry will time out even if a later attempt succeeds. That is a functional regression in the email retry path and fails VAL-AS-005.

sharedStateObservations.observation: There is a scope mismatch between the feature definition and VAL-AS-003: the feature description/expected behavior only target six actor `Receive` handlers, while the validation contract text says every actor and grain default case should use `ctx.Unhandled()`. That makes it unclear whether grain `bad_request` handlers are intended behavior or validation failures.
